options: Energy transferred when a force moves an object
Studying or going to a job
Pushing hard, even if nothing moves
questions.explanation: Work is the energy a force transfers to an object it actually moves — no motion means zero work.
questions.misconception: Everyday 'effort' is not physics work; a push without movement does no work at all.

questions.prompt: You push a cart 2 m with a force of 10 N. How much work did you do?
questions.misconception: Using only force (10) or squaring values gives 200 J; the force × distance product is the recipe.

questions.prompt: You push a heavy cabinet with all your strength, but it does not budge. How much work did the push do on it?
options: A lot, then it becomes heat
Exactly as much as your effort
It depends on your tired arms
questions.explanation: Work needs distance: force with zero motion transfers zero energy — no distance, no work.
questions.misconception: Effort and work are different; physics 'work' requires the object to actually move.

questions.prompt: The work you do on a cart shows up in the cart as...
options: An equal gain of kinetic energy
questions.explanation: The work a force does on an object becomes that object's kinetic energy — same value in joules.
questions.misconception: Imagining work as 'used up' rather than transferred; it lands in the cart as motion.

questions.prompt: What is force × distance measured in?
questions.explanation: Work is energy, and energy is measured in joules.
questions.misconception: Newtons measure the force input and watts measure power; work keeps the joule.
